themes_detail.label: Indoor Air Quality Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Indoor air quality complaints spiked to 7 THIS WEEK, a 154% increase from the 2.8-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.43), suggesting a sudden environmental or building-system failure affecting multiple Bushwick residences.
evidence: 7 indoor air quality complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.8 weekly average (154% spike, z-score 6.43)
Spike is most recent signal in dataset; emerged within last 7 days
Statistically significant deviation indicates acute rather than chronic issue
reporting_angles: Interview residents in affected buildings to identify common symptoms or location patterns
Contact DEP and DOB to determine if inspection complaints trace to specific HVAC failures, mold outbreaks, or nearby commercial pollution sources

themes_detail.label: Damaged Street Signs Surge
themes_detail.summary: Street sign damage complaints reached 3 THIS WEEK, a 500% spike from the 0.5-complaint weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 5.0), indicating accelerated infrastructure decay or vandalism in public right-of-way.
evidence: 3 damaged street sign complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average (500% increase, z-score 5.0)
Emerged within past 7 days alongside other infrastructure concerns
Convergence with Dead/Dying Tree spike (3 complaints last week, 700% increase) suggests broader infrastructure maintenance gap
reporting_angles: Map complaint locations to identify geographic hotspot (single block vs. district-wide pattern)
Interview DOT about maintenance schedule and resource allocation for Bushwick vs. neighboring districts

themes_detail.label: Illegal Animal Sales Network
themes_detail.summary: Illegal animal sales complaints jumped to 4 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 3100% spike from the 0.1-complaint weekly average (z-score: 11.72), suggesting organized trafficking or unregulated breeders operating in Bushwick.
evidence: 4 illegal animal sales complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (3100% spike, z-score 11.72)
Highest z-score in dataset; indicates extreme statistical anomaly
Species and seller identity unknown; requires ground reporting to determine if organized network vs. isolated incidents
reporting_angles: Identify which neighborhoods/blocks complaints originated from; canvass for active illegal sales operations
Interview ASPCA and NYPD about enforcement priorities and whether this reflects a known trafficking corridor

themes_detail.label: Hazardous Materials Spike
themes_detail.summary: Hazardous materials complaints spiked to 4 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 3100% increase from the 0.1-complaint weekly average (z-score: 11.72), potentially indicating industrial dumping, construction violations, or chemical storage breaches.
evidence: 4 hazardous materials complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (3100% spike, z-score 11.72)
Tied with illegal animal sales as highest statistical anomaly in dataset
Aligns with community board's repeated DEP green infrastructure requests, suggesting environmental infrastructure gaps
reporting_angles: Obtain complaint details: substance type, location, suspected source (industrial, construction, household)
Cross-reference with active ULURP projects (150 Noll, 460 Troutman, 132 Melrose) to determine if construction-related hazmat handling is implicated

themes_detail.label: Non-Emergency Police Calls Surge
themes_detail.summary: Non-emergency police complaints jumped to 18 LAST WEEK, a 243% increase from the 5.2-complaint weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 4.93), suggesting rising quality-of-life or low-level crime concerns residents are escalating to NYPD.
evidence: 18 non-emergency police complaints last week vs. 5.2 weekly average (243% spike, z-score 4.93)
Spike emerged last week; remains high but specific call types unavailable in dataset
Convergence with noise complaints (1451 total over 90 days, persistent concern) and parking violations (1431) suggests disorder/quality-of-life triggers
reporting_angles: Request NYPD incident reports or 311 complaint narratives to categorize nature of calls (noise-related, trespassing, loitering, street activity)
Conduct street-level reporting in high-complaint blocks to assess actual disorder vs. resident perception shift
